annotations.text:
AllSport dashboard redesign — round 2, your critique applied.

SCREENS (top row) · SYSTEM SPECS (bottom row)

The dashboard is now four blocks: identity, taniwha card, four numbers, skill radar. Everything below moved into Taniwha History, which is what the card opens.

Limb artwork is filler geometry so the assembly reads — twelve real drawings, ten registered layers each, still to come.

TANIWHA CARD — what changed

· "Currently earning" label
· Name + English gloss
· Tap for Taniwha History
· The creature assembling, limb by limb
· 5 of 10 limbs, currently building Ringa Matau (right arm)
· Three numbers at once: this taniwha, this limb, all time
· Bottom text and the choose button are GONE — the button now lives in Taniwha History

SKILL RADAR

Ten spokes, one per domain, in the ten domain colours. Each spoke is the player's average Top % in that domain — further out is stronger. Strongest and weakest are named underneath so the shape never has to be decoded.

A new player's shape sits near the centre and grows outward, which is the right story.
Opens from the taniwha card. Holds the choose/switch control, the limbs earned with dates, the play history you moved off the dashboard, and the colours era.
Retitled MY TANIWHA. Four counts across the top, then each taniwha as an expandable row — expanded here to show all ten named limbs and what the crown needs.
Lens toggle dropped. Every event now shows PR, average placement and wins side by side, and the strongest-to-weakest bars at the top answer "what am I good at" before any domain is opened.
The bottom bar is fixed — it travels with the screen on every page, sitting above the content on a shadow rather than at the end of it.

RESOLVED SINCE ROUND 2 — the particle is unmacronised: "Te Taniwha o te …" across all twelve, in the canvas and in lib/taniwha.ts.

STILL OPEN — (1) the English glosses are mine except Connection, which is yours. (2) Hiko, Manawanui, Mataara and Ruruku are the four names still awaiting a reo speaker, along with the Hiko/Hiku, Kaha/Kaha Tinana and Manawanui/Manawaroa near-collisions. (3) Taniwha artwork: Tāne is drawing the twelve in Canva — ten registered layers each, exported as {slug}/{limb}.png.
SYSTEM SPECS — states, sizes and the failure modes each piece is designed against.
